- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral, model often underestimates, especially after sharp drops; adjust downward bias or add lagged support.
- After a spike in price or sentiment, model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction to dampen upward trend.
- Model consistently underestimates true price after a 30-day forecast horizon; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply mean reversion heuristic with 3–5 day smoothing.
- When true outcome shows strong reversal after a peak, model fails to anticipate; add early warning signal if sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days.
